# The learned boundary-integral model {#sec-learned-bie}

The layer-potential controls of the architectural-ablation study — the
gated model-selection study behind the moment-decoder diagnosis of
@sec-ceiling (checked-in `results/architectural_ablation_2026-07-01.json`)
— left a sharp question open. An 8-parameter learned Richardson solve
feeding the *analytic* double-layer kernel passed every prespecified gate
(ID $0.0235$,
frequency-OOD $0.071$, under the ablation study's own protocol — the
ladder protocol below re-baselines the analytic oracle at 0.003/0.060,
@tbl-h1e), while free-form learned kernels with thousands of
parameters had excellent supervised values but no operator fidelity
(Laplacian residuals of 8–10, frequency-OOD of 0.6–0.9). Which ingredient
carries the operator generalization — the **density-solve/propagation
factorization**, or the **analytic kernel**? This chapter answers by
falsification: neither alone.

## The falsification ladder {#sec-ladder}

All ladder runs: seed 17, 1,000 updates unless noted, early 8-case evaluation
bank; numbers from the research log and the `hypothesis_chain` block of the
checked-in `results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`. The control is the
free-form invariant pair kernel ("p0": an MLP of the joint invariants
$(|r|^2, n\cdot r)$, 19,008 parameters), with ID 0.091, frequency-OOD 0.605,
normalized Laplacian residual 8.0.

**H1 — the factorization alone (refuted).** Tie one MLP kernel into both a
$p{=}8$ drive-linear Richardson solve through $\tilde T = \tfrac12 I +
\tilde K_\kappa$ and the propagation sum (the diagonal $\tfrac12$ is a gauge:
rescaling $(\beta,\kappa) \to (c\beta, c\kappa)$ leaves tied propagation
invariant). All contracts hold to $3\times10^{-7}$. Result: ID 0.154,
frequency-OOD **0.756 — worse than the control**. The trajectories are
identical to step 500, after which the control keeps improving and the
BIE-wrapped model stalls. Diagnosis: architecture alone exerts no gradient
pressure toward trace consistency; a fixed-$\alpha$ Richardson filter is just
a reparameterization the propagation kernel must invert.

**H1b — trace loss (refuted) and H1c — soft kernel-PDE penalty (refuted).**
Add dimensionless auxiliary losses at equal weight: H1b penalizes the model's
own trace residual $\tilde T\mu - \tilde g$; H1c penalizes the kernel's
harmonicity defect $\operatorname{mean}((|r|^2\,\nabla^2_x\kappa)^2)$ using
only the PDE operator (closed form
$\nabla^2\kappa = 4a\kappa_{aa} + 4b\kappa_{ab} + \kappa_{bb} + 4\kappa_a$
in the invariants, verified against ambient autograd). Each penalty moves its
own diagnostic and nothing else:

| model | ID | freq-OOD | trace | Laplacian |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| p0 control | 0.091 | 0.605 | 0.150 | 7.998 |
| H1c: + kernel-PDE penalty | **0.083** | 0.706 | 0.352 | 3.474 |
| H1b: BIE + trace loss | 0.142 | 0.735 | **0.078** | 6.571 |
| H1b+c: both | 0.195 | 0.680 | 0.060 | 2.782 |

: Soft penalties optimize their own metric, not generalization (seed 17, early bank). {#tbl-soft}

The maximum-principle mechanism needs the Laplacian residual to be *exactly*
zero, not twice better; soft penalties at equal weight simply fight the data
fit.

**H1d — exact harmonicity, midpoint quadrature (refuted, instructively).**
Replace the MLP by the exactly harmonic Laurent family @eq-laurent (real
coefficients, per-source expansion, coincident-safe). Under midpoint
quadrature it *loses badly*: ID 0.652, frequency-OOD 1.014 — worse than the
free-form MLP it replaced. Two lessons with teeth:

1. **A self-declared trace metric is vacuous for a converged solve.** The BIE
   variant reaches trace residual 0.002 with Laplacian $\approx 0$ — and ID
   0.65. Richardson drives $\tilde T\mu \to \tilde g$ *by definition* for any
   kernel; the collocation residual certifies solver convergence, and
   certifies boundary fidelity only when the imposed jump matches the
   kernel's actual jump (the self-consistent point $c_1 = -1/2\pi$).
2. **Singular kernels demand singular quadrature.** The free-form MLP wins
   in-sample by learning a *mollified* near field that absorbs
   midpoint-quadrature error next to panels; exactly singular Laurent terms
   cannot mollify, so the optimizer suppresses $c_1$ to avoid near-boundary
   error spikes.

**H1e — exact harmonic basis + exact panel quadrature + learned solve
(confirmed).** On a straight panel, $\zeta$ is affine in arclength with unit
slope, so *every* Laurent term integrates in closed form,

$$
\int_{\text{panel}} \operatorname{Re}F(\zeta)\, ds
= -\sigma\,\operatorname{Im}\bigl[G(\zeta_{\text{end}})
  - G(\zeta_{\text{start}})\bigr],
\qquad G' = F,\quad \sigma = n\times\tau ,
$$

and the singular term reduces to the **signed subtended angle**
$-\sigma\, c_1\operatorname{atan2}(\mathrm{cross},\mathrm{dot})$ (the factor
$\sigma$ matters: the subtended angle is $n$-independent but the integral is
odd in $n$ — caught by a brute-force quadrature test). The analytic oracle is
*the exact member* $c_1 = -1/2\pi,\ d = 0$, verified to machine precision.
This is `HarmonicPanelBIE` in `self_consistent_kernel.py`: 5 kernel
coefficients + 8 relaxations = 13 parameters, initialized at
$\mathcal N(0, 10^{-2})$ — *not* seeded at the analytic value.

| model | params | ID | geo | strong | freq | trace | Laplacian |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| p0 MLP control | 19,008 | 0.091 | 0.101 | 0.124 | 0.605 | 0.150 | 8.0 |
| panel basis, direct (no solve) | 5 | 0.213 | 0.222 | 0.194 | 0.352 | 0.359 | $\approx 0$ |
| **panel basis + BIE solve** | **13** | **0.035** | **0.038** | **0.055** | **0.090** | 0.0004 | $\approx 0$ |
| analytic Richardson oracle | 8 | 0.003 | 0.003 | 0.026 | 0.060 | 0.0005 | $\approx 0$ |

: H1e confirmed (seed 17, 1,000 updates, early bank). The frequency-OOD gap closes from 0.605 to 0.090, at the analytic operator's own level. {#tbl-h1e}

The learned $c_1$ is $-0.1513$ against $-1/2\pi = -0.1592$ (5%) from
random init, on interior supervision alone; at 3,000 steps it reaches
$-0.15801$ (0.7%) with ID 0.0062 — the 1,000-step gap was optimization, not
representation. The ablations support this chain:

> **operator generalization = PDE-conforming kernel *basis* (exactly
> harmonic, containing the true kernel) + exact singular *quadrature* +
> learned drive-linear density *solve* — each necessary, none sufficient.**

## The learned kernel is the double layer

The claim in this section's title is checked visually and numerically:
the three learned scalars converge onto the classical interior
double-layer kernel, with $c_1$ within 0.8% of $-1/2\pi$ on every seed.
This is the strongest form of interpretability the program has — the
learned object *is* a known object of potential theory — and it is what
licenses classical acceleration (FMM, $\mathcal H$-matrices) downstream:
the acceleration methods developed for the analytic kernel apply unchanged to the
learned one. The training trajectories below show the same convergence
dynamically, including the Neumann model's slow kernel–solve
co-adaptation.

![The learned 3-parameter kernel member against the analytic interior
double-layer kernel $-\frac{1}{2\pi}\frac{n\cdot r}{|r|^2}$, as a function of
the joint invariants: angular profile at $|r|=1$ (left), radial decay along
$\psi = 0$ (center), and the learned $c_1$ for all three seeds on the
reference bank against $-1/2\pi$ (right). Left/center evaluate the seed-17
session checkpoint; right panel is from the checked-in results
JSON.](figures/kernel_learned_vs_analytic.png){#fig-kernel}

![Validation trajectories (session artifacts under `/tmp`, not checked in;
validation uses the deployment discretization of 128 panels / 512 queries).
Left: Dirichlet — the pruned 3-parameter model and the 13-parameter model
cross below the 19k-parameter MLP control before step 1,000 and keep

## Pruning: two scalars carry the operator {#sec-pruning}

Pruning the 13-parameter model at the 3,000-step budget (seed 17,
early bank; checked-in `iteration_4_pruning`) gives:

| variant | params | ID | geo | strong | freq | trace |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| full (5 coeffs + 8 relaxations) | 13 | 0.0062 | 0.0066 | 0.0297 | 0.0618 | 0.0004 |
| minimal (drop $d_1..d_3$) | 10 | 0.0056 | 0.0058 | 0.0277 | 0.0612 | 0.0004 |
| **shared relaxation** | **3** | **0.0056** | 0.0058 | 0.0277 | 0.0612 | 0.0004 |
| $p{=}2$ solve | 4 | 0.0067 | 0.0139 | 0.0403 | 0.0612 | **0.0653** |

: Pruning ablations. Sharing the relaxation is lossless to four decimals. {#tbl-pruning}

Sharing the relaxation across the 8 Richardson steps is lossless — every
converged run had learned a uniform relaxation anyway. The learned values:
$c_1 = -0.15828$ (0.5% from $-1/2\pi$), $d_0 = -0.0015 \approx 0$, $\alpha =
1.180$: effectively **two scalars carry the interior Dirichlet Laplace
solution operator**. Cutting the solve to $p{=}2$ degrades the trace
160$\times$ and the kernel inflates ($c_1 = -0.1705$) to compensate — solve
depth is a numerical-convergence knob, like quadrature order, not prunable
capacity.

The three-seed confirmation on the frozen 64-case reference bank (3,000
steps) is the program's headline row:

| metric | 3-param BIE | MeshTransformer (136k) | pair kernel (19k) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| ID relative $L^2$ | **0.0347 ± 0.0006** | 0.458 | 0.107 |
| unseen geometry | 0.0343 ± 0.0007 | — | — |
| stronger deformation | 0.0302 ± 0.0006 | — | — |
| unseen frequencies | **0.0664 ± 0.0004** | 1.000 | 0.642 |
| boundary trace | 0.0003 | — | — |
| Laplacian residual | 0.0001 | 0.401 | 9.76 |
| $c_1$ by seed | −0.15828 / −0.15825 / −0.15790 | | |

: Three seeds, frozen reference bank, evaluation seed 97000037 (checked-in JSONs: `learned_bie_2026-07-02` for the BIE and same-bank comparisons; baseline Laplacians from `reference_2026-07-01`). Seed spread is ~30× tighter than any larger variant; $c_1$ is within 0.8% of $-1/2\pi$ on every seed. {#tbl-headline}

## Resolution transfer: converging like a numerical method

Because the learned coefficients are resolution-independent and the
quadrature is exact, the model trained at 64 panels *improves* monotonically
under boundary refinement — discretization-convergent learning:

```{python}
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Evaluation error versus boundary panel count for the seed-17 model
#|   trained at 64 panels (checked-in learned_bie_2026-07-02.json,
#|   resolution_transfer_seed17). Error decreases monotonically under
#|   refinement to 4x the training resolution.
import json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

results = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" / "learned_bie_2026-07-02.json"))
transfer = results["resolution_transfer_seed17"]["relative_l2_by_n_boundary"]
panels = sorted(int(k) for k in transfer)
errors = [transfer[str(p)] for p in panels]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5.6, 3.2))
ax.plot(panels, errors, "-o", color="#2a78d6", lw=2, ms=7)
for p, e in zip(panels, errors):
    ax.annotate(f"{e:.3f}", (p, e), textcoords="offset points", xytext=(8, 4),
                fontsize=8.5, color="#52514e")
ax.axvline(64, color="#c3c2b7", lw=1.2, ls=":")
ax.text(65.5, 0.0405, "training\nresolution", fontsize=8, color="#898781",
        va="bottom")
ax.set_xscale("log", base=2)
ax.set_yscale("log")
ax.set_xticks(panels, [str(p) for p in panels])
ax.set_xlabel("boundary panels at evaluation")
ax.set_ylabel(r"relative $L^2$")
ax.grid(True, color="#e1e0d9", lw=0.8)
for spine in ("top", "right"):
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

Contracts hold exactly throughout: superposition to $10^{-7}$, similarity
covariance to $2\times10^{-6}$, exact query independence, harmonicity by
construction.

## Neumann boundary conditions {#sec-neumann}

Does the recipe transfer to a different BC/jump structure? The Neumann
problem trains on exact analytic flux data (compatibility-corrected, targets
gauge-fixed to the boundary-measure mean; see @sec-pde-theory).
`NeumannHarmonicPanelBIE` extends the kernel family with the single-layer
term $c_0 \operatorname{Re}\log\zeta$ (branch-safe exact panel integrals,
including the finite self-panel value $L(\log(L/2)-1)$) and obtains the
Neumann trace $K' = n\cdot\nabla(\text{influence})$ by exact autograd
differentiation of the panel integrals — no new quadrature.

**Round 1 exposed a structural failure mode.** With the textbook interior
orientation $\tilde T = -\tfrac12 I + \tilde K'$ and relaxation initialized
at $+1$, the trained model looked healthy in-sample (ID 0.081) — but its
learned kernel was *zero* ($c_0 = -0.008$ vs oracle magnitude $0.159$).
At zero kernel each Richardson step multiplies the density by
$(1 + \alpha/2) \approx 1.49$; eight steps make a $\sim$25$\times$
amplifier. SGD had exploited **solver divergence as gain** instead of
learning physics. The fix is a gauge choice, not tuning: adopt the $c=-1$
gauge $\tilde T = +\tfrac12 I + \tilde K'$ with oracle $c_0 = -1/2\pi$,
placing the zero-kernel initialization inside the convergent regime. (The
first attempted flip, $\tfrac12 I - \tilde K'$, is *not* the gauge transform
and has no self-consistent point — the analytic-oracle test caught it, and
also caught that the test itself had hard-coded the old convention.)

**Round 2 transfers, slowly.** The landscape has an early barrier while
kernel and solve co-adapt (@fig-convergence, right): validation rises to
$\sim$3.4 by step 250 before descending; convergence is $\sim$3× slower than
Dirichlet. Results (seed 17, checked-in `iteration_2_neumann`):

| steps | ID | geo | strong | freq-OOD | Laplacian | learned $c_0$ |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1,000 | 0.962 (mid-transit) | | | | | |
| 3,000 | 0.1234 | 0.1217 | 0.1578 | 0.1236 | $10^{-5}$ | −0.1431 (90% of oracle) |
| **10,000** | **0.0029** | 0.0043 | 0.0044 | **0.0021** | $2\times10^{-5}$ | **−0.1619 (1.8% from $-1/2\pi$)** |

: Neumann closeout, seed 17. At 10k steps: analytic-oracle-level accuracy uniformly across all splits, including unseen frequencies. The direct (no-solve) control shows the value-interpolator signature instead: ID 0.122, freq-OOD 0.658. Seeds 29/43 at 3,000 steps sit at 0.27/0.19 — the same slow transit seed 17 showed at 3,000 (0.12); the 10k run establishes the destination. {#tbl-neumann}

Note that freq-OOD $\approx$ ID at every converged checkpoint — uniform
operator behavior. The verdict: **changing the boundary
condition costs optimization time, not structure**, with two durable design
rules for learned second-kind solvers — (1) the orientation gauge must make
the zero-kernel initialization solver-convergent, and (2) budget for a
co-adaptation barrier in learned-solve landscapes.

## Under the product scope

Read against the problem statement in the front matter — the governing
equations are *not given* in deployment — the ladder's findings take a
sharper meaning. Free-form learned kernels are **value interpolators**:
excellent supervised accuracy, no operator fidelity (frequency-OOD 0.6–0.9,
Laplacian residuals of 8–10). Exact PDE-conforming structure wins decisively
wherever it is available — but it was available here only because the
benchmark was selected because its PDE is known. The 3-parameter model
is therefore an **oracle-in-family diagnostic**, not a deployable recipe:
it establishes the ceiling that structure sets and identifies which
ingredients are essential. What *does* carry over unconditionally is the
PDE-agnostic part of the chain (@sec-pde-agnostic): the factorization, the
second-kind solve with its gauge rule, and the singular-quadrature
discipline. The open question the ladder sharpens for the unknown-PDE
setting is how close a **learned singularity-dictionary kernel** — a
dictionary spanning log/power singular parts plus smooth corrections, exact
quadrature per member, no member privileged — can come to this oracle from
data alone, without being told the PDE. That is the top-ranked direction of
@sec-future.
